name: auth_sdk
_comment: The auth module's Next.js half (deliveryplatform wave). Carries the whole NextAuth surface a shell needs to authenticate against the platform: the app/(auth) route group (credentials login/register/forgot-password + the [...nextauth] handler), the always-paas PaaSLogin form, the drizzle/Postgres persistence the credential flow writes to (db/, lib/drizzle/, drizzle.config.ts), and the four seam files it overwrites in the host: middleware.ts (NextAuth-gated), app/lib/session.ts (NextAuth-backed session seam), app/services/control/global_settings.ts (drizzle-backed GlobalSettings store) and components/custom/session-provider.tsx (the client-side next-auth/react SessionProvider wrapper that base_sdk's useSession() callers - app-sidebar.tsx, nav/team-switcher.tsx - need mounted above them; the host's own app/layout.tsx imports it and wraps <body> children with it, exactly as RokctAI_frontend's layout does). The bare shell commits neutral no-auth copies of those seams (for session-provider.tsx a pass-through that just renders children), so it builds green without this SDK; composing auth_sdk swaps in the real implementations. The root route app/(chat)/page.tsx is owned by agent_sdk (its installer copies the whole app/(chat) group), not by this SDK. Since 1.6.0 the credentials flow's THREE tenant-mapping operations sit behind a one-marker first-wins registry, app/(auth)/tenant-link.ts (// @rokct-sdk-tenant-link-start, `{ id: "<sdk>-tenant-link", load: () => import("@/app/(auth)/<file>") },`): resolving which tenant site an email signs in against, remembering the keys and site a login produced, and naming the administrator a registration provisions under. The local Postgres store those used to read and write inline is a MULTI-TENANCY feature - it maps a user to the base URL they came from - so it stays the DEFAULT, moved verbatim into app/(auth)/tenant-link-database.ts and selected whenever nothing is registered and ROKCT_TENANT_LINK is unset: rokctai_frontend reads and writes Postgres exactly as before. A shell dedicated to ONE tenant selects app/(auth)/tenant-link-single.ts instead with `ROKCT_TENANT_LINK=single-tenant` (its own next.config.mjs `env` is the host-owned, compose-durable place for that); it resolves the site from base_sdk's kernel resolver (app/services/base/tenant-hosts.ts envBaseUrl(), hence the new `requires` entry), reads the administrator from ROKCT_ADMIN_API_KEY / ROKCT_ADMIN_API_SECRET, and makes both local writes no-ops - so app/(auth)/auth.ts and app/(auth)/actions.ts carry no `db.` call at all any more and a single-tenant deployment opens no database connection on login or register. Since 1.7.0 (requires base_sdk >= 1.20.0) the SDK carries the TENANT-HOST SWITCH and the REGISTER REGISTRY. The switch: middleware.ts asks base_sdk's resolveTenantSiteForRequest (app/services/base/tenant-host-control.ts, hence the new requires entry) which tenant site the request host belongs to; with nothing resolved (the platform's own domain, a preview, a local run, an unclaimed domain) the request is handed to NextAuth exactly as before, and with a site it goes on with the x-rokct-tenant-site request header set, / and /landing are rewritten to /login, /register is redirected to /login, and every other path keeps the path/role logic (NextAuth's gate runs first on every path; the switch only reshapes its pass-through answers). app/(auth)/login/page.tsx is now a server switch: with a site_name query parameter (it wins) or the header it renders the tenant portal login (components/custom/paas-login.tsx, which posts to https://<site> and nowhere else), otherwise the platform's own sign-in (login/login-view.tsx, the client page it used to be); the login action falls back to the header when the form named no site. Unknown hosts never render a portal against the control site. app/(auth)/tenant-host.ts holds the pure decision (TENANT_LOGIN_PATH, TENANT_HOME_PATHS, TENANT_REGISTER_PATHS, tenantHostDecision, resolveTenantSite). The registry (Ray, 2026-09-09: 'register is not fitting for all, what rokct need is not what all needs, any home sdk need to inject what it needs, just like dart auth sdk has'): the Dart auth SDK owns the register FLOW and the home SDK injects the rest (AuthRegistrationConfig flags at // @auth-registration-config, registration_steps at @generated-registration-steps, completion at @registration-complete-hook). Mirrored here as two one-marker single-answer registries in the tenant-link.ts shape. components/custom/auth/register-registry.ts (// @rokct-sdk-register-start, `{ id: "<sdk>-register", load: () => import("@/components/custom/auth/<file>") },`) takes a RegisterConfig: enabled (false: the register page redirects to TENANT_LOGIN_PATH), copy (title, subtitle, cta, signInPrompt, signInLabel), fields (RegisterField: name, label, type text|email|password|tel|url|number|select|checkbox|hidden, placeholder, required, defaultValue, fromQuery, autoComplete, hint, options, loadOptions, span) rendered after the account fields, and steps (RegisterStep: id, label, skippable, load -> a component taking next, skip, email, siteName) run one after another once the account exists. app/(auth)/register-provision.ts (// @rokct-sdk-register-provision-start, `{ id: "<sdk>-register-provision", load: () => import("@/app/(auth)/<file>") },`) takes a RegisterProvisioner whose provision(submission: email, password, firstName, lastName, values, tenantSite) answers a RegisterOutcome (success with optional signIn and message, or failed | user_exists | invalid_data with error); a separate server-side file so no server module is reachable from the client-safe config. With NOTHING registered: auth_sdk's own register page (first name, last name, email, password; the platform's words) and the default provisioner app/(auth)/register-provision-default.ts, the platform's guest api.user.register_user on the tenant site the request is for (the Dart AuthRepository's own sign-up call) followed by a sign-in - never the control site. Everything rokct-specific that register() and auth-form.tsx carried inline until 1.6.0 - company and tenant provisioning at the control site under a platform administrator's keys (control:provision_service_subscription / control:provision_new_tenant), the plan choice and ?plan= prefill, the industry catalogue (getIndustries, gone), the country and currency lookup (get_pricing_metadata), the voucher and the service domain - is OUT of auth_sdk and is what agent_sdk injects through these two registries in a later release; lib/actions/getSubscriptionPlans.ts is still installed (other files may import it) but nothing in auth_sdk reads it any more. README.md carries the contract and a worked example.

integrations._comment: The drizzle migration scripts travel with the drizzle config/schema this SDK installs; the bare shell's package.json carries neither. Inserted after the host's lint script line (idempotent: skipped when already present).
